scope: All open and closed issues and comments returned by the repository API: 2 open issues, 1 comment; page 2 empty. Pull requests excluded.
authority: Discussion is reviewed against the pinned published specification; no maintainer acceptance or adopted errata is inferred.

findings.topic: DPart child arrays and parent links
findings.decision: Keep the array-of-arrays and correct Parent requirements. The historical sample defect is repaired in current creation code.
findings.source: ISO 32000-2 document parts, as required by EA-PDF sections 9.2 and 9.6.
findings.evidence: Java DocumentPartChecks; Python check_dpart_object_structure; DPart parent, array and page-range regressions.

findings.decision: Delegate the PDF/A determination to veraPDF on the finished file. Do not infer that a proposed future standards amendment is already effective.
findings.source: PDF/A prerequisite; this is not a new custom EA-PDF rule.
findings.evidence: Current real outputs are independently checked by veraPDF. No blanket font stripping is introduced.

findings.decision: Separate recommended presence, mandatory format when supplied, and actual digest agreement. PDF CheckSum is 16 binary bytes; XMP uses 32 hexadecimal characters.
findings.evidence: PdfMailWriter.setEmbeddedChecksum; both validators check binary encoding and payload digest; malformed checksum regressions.

findings.topic: Tags must refer to actual content
findings.decision: Retain content, MCID, ParentTree and ownership checks. Merely having a structure tree is insufficient. A few linked tags do not establish accessibility certification.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.7 and applicable ISO/TS 32005 requirements.
findings.evidence: Creator PreservationRegressionTests and MarkedContentRepairTests; Python check_structure_correspondence; Java LogicalStructureChecks/PageContentChecks.

findings.decision: Retain the published EA-PDF requirement. The concern that viewers ignore it is recorded; discussion is not an adopted deletion of the requirement. Preserve the separately labelled PDF 1.7 collection interpretation.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.1, printed pages 62–63; linked pdf-association/report-an-issue#14.
findings.evidence: Both validators and creator retain profile-specific settings. Existing source-review decisions distinguish PDF behaviour from EA-PDF file requirements.

findings.decision: Accept omitted End as Start. Reject invalid ranges and follow the prescribed single-page omission.
findings.evidence: Java DocumentPartChecks defaults End to Start; Python page_range_from_dpart does likewise; single-page and reversed-range tests pass.

findings.decision: Resolved: accept a single root whose resolved standard role is Document. Literal /S spelling alone must not decide the result.
findings.evidence: Java StructureRolesTests and Python test_role_mapping_review cover transitive mapping, invalid targets, cycles and bounds. This supersedes the open item in the 29 October issue review.

findings.topic: PDF 2 namespace mappings and legacy compatibility
findings.decision: Resolve explicit NS through RoleMapNS and implicit namespace through the applicable RoleMap. Keep the separately required legacy compatibility map; PDF 2 ignoring it for an explicitly namespaced element does not remove EA-PDF compatibility requirements.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.7 and Tables 9–10, printed 74–75; ISO 32000-2 section14.8.6.2.
findings.evidence: Both role resolvers test explicit NS overriding a conflicting root map. Full-map versus used-tag scope remains a labelled project interpretation, not adopted errata.

findings.decision: Retain all three namespace/prefix requirements. The issue claim that pdfmail is absent from the specification conflicts with the pinned document.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.8 printed 83 explicitly requires the following namespaces; Table 14 printed 84 lists pdfmail, pdfmailid and pdfmailmeta.
findings.evidence: Re-read the complete preceding SHALL sentence and Table 14, not only the schema sections. Both validators retain the requirement.

findings.decision: Accept creator names for people, organizations or services; do not demand a software product name or reject address-like spelling. Separate first-item/type checks from provenance.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.8 printed 84; standard Dublin Core/XMP creator meaning.
findings.evidence: CreationProvenanceTests; both validators report unknown attribution as unavailable rather than infer it from punctuation or equality with the sender.

findings.decision: The pinned specification expressly names the EA-PDF file creation date. Retain that meaning, but do not claim that timestamp syntax or a comparison with Sent proves the actual creation event.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.8 printed 84: creation-software obligation for EA-PDF file creation date.
findings.evidence: Both validators separate XMP date format from independent provenance. The comment questioning whether the SHALL exists is contradicted by the published clause.

findings.decision: Retain a qualifying attachment annotation in every relevant email-body content set. An AttachmentList can be additional navigation; it does not replace the body requirement. Presence and visibility/CropBox are now independently reported.
findings.source: EA-PDF section 9.3 printed 65; last note explicitly leaves attachment indexes unconstrained by this requirement.
findings.evidence: Both validators bind annotations to the owning body set. The clipped-icon regression passes presence and fails visibility.

findings.topic: Revision, ISO 32005, GUID and tag nesting
findings.decision: Keep revision 2024 and the applicable ISO 32005 assessment. Verify GUID on the actual owning message and correct structure ancestry, rather than accepting an identifier found somewhere else.
findings.source: EA-PDF Table 15 printed 84 and section 9.7; linked pdf-association/report-an-issue#21.
findings.evidence: Current creator/validators retain these checks. Independent ISO 32005 assessment is separate from PDF/A and custom rule coverage.

findings.decision: The attachment URL returns HTTP 404. Its bytes could not be retrieved, so the updated sample has not been tested. Existing compare/bfo.pdf has revision 2025 and is not treated as the updated revision 2024 sample.
findings.evidence: Historical compare/bfo.pdf and compare/uiuc.pdf were separately tested without changes. Both pass PDF/A and fail EA-PDF checks; both now pass resolved Document-root checks. Final reports retain their other failures. Neither file is represented as the unavailable updated attachment.

validation_evidence: Standalone Java 229-rule reports: output/rule-refinement-2026-10-31/evidence/java/thirdparty-229/. Both historical third-party PDFs pass PDF/A but fail EA-PDF; input hashes unchanged.
